questions: Should the plot's x-axis be indices (0,1,2,...) or something else (e.g., original positions)?
Is the plot expected to have any labels, title, or grid, or is a bare line plot sufficient?
If the flattened list is empty (e.g., L=[] or L=[[],[]]), what should be returned? An empty plot? Raise an error?
Should the standardized data be plotted as a line connecting points, or as markers/scatter?
Is the order of flattened elements preserved as per chain(*L) (row-major), or should it be column-major or sorted?
Should the function close the plot figure before returning (to avoid display in interactive environments)?
Are sublists guaranteed to contain only integers, or could they contain floats? Should non-integers be handled?
Should the plot y-axis represent standardized_data as a 1D array or as is (2D column)? Reference uses 2D input to plot, which plots each column as a line; if multiple columns, behavior changes.
